candidates.name: American mahjong boom (clubs, classes, game nights)
candidates.summary: A surge of mostly young adult and women newcomers learning mahjong (especially the American/NMJL style) through clubs, paid classes and hosted game nights.
candidates.what: Mahjong is a tile game that originated in 19th-century China; the American variant uses an annual card of hands issued by the National Mah Jongg League. Since about 2023 it has become a social 'girls' night', bar-night and club activity across the US, with paid beginner classes, clubs and themed sets/merch. Newcomers need to learn tiles, the Charleston and scoring, and organizers need ways to run tables, leagues and classes.

origin.text: The game is centuries-old Chinese tradition; the current US wave shows up in Eventbrite data as a 179% rise in mahjong events from 2023 to 2024 and accelerated through 2025-2026.

adopters.text: Young adults and Gen Z, many women hosting 'girls' night' games, plus Asian-American players reconnecting with family tradition; club founders, bars and new independent instructors teaching paid classes.

spread.text: Independent coverage across national outlets (NPR via WBUR syndication, PBS NewsHour, NBC, Boston Globe), regional press in Utah, Colorado, Philadelphia, the tri-state area and the Southeast, plus wire coverage abroad. Event platforms (Eventbrite, Evite) and Yelp independently report growth.

trajectory.text: Still accelerating into fall 2026: Yelp club searches up ~4,500% YoY (reported April 2026), Evite events reported up 94% YoY, and August 2026 coverage still describes rapid expansion. No source found describing a decline; appropriation criticism is recurring but has not slowed adoption in the evidence seen.

productDemand.text: Purchase intent is visible for physical goods (official card bundles estimated ~6,000/month on Amazon in July 2026; gift guides and trade press on mahjong gifts) and for learning/organizing aids: third-party keyword estimates show 'mahjong pdf' +89%, 'mahjong group' +83% and 'mahjong instructor' +556%, and classes are oversubscribed. Etsy printables show view activity but sales were not observed.

competition.text: High for generic products: many Etsy beginner cheat sheets ($1-$12), 2026 score cards and hand trackers, suit-pun totes, plus mass-market advent calendars and gift-guide merch. Not checked (search budget ran out): how many listings target instructors or club/league organizers specifically.

gap.text: Generic player cheat sheets are crowded, so the opening is likely the supply side of the boom: new instructors (searches rising fast) and club/league organizers need class handouts, sign-in and progress sheets, table-rotation charts, standings and kitty/payout ledgers, which player-focused printables do not cover. A beginner guide that credits the game's Chinese origins and covers several variants (Chinese/HK, American, Riichi) would also stand apart from card-centric sheets. Whether instructor kits are already crowded is unverified.

window.estimate: Now through Dec 2026 for holiday hosting and gifting; organizer/instructor tools likely stay relevant through 2027.
window.reasoning: Growth is multi-year and still accelerating; digital delivery is instant, so the November-December hosting/gift window is reachable even with slow listing discovery. Clubs and classes recruit again in January and around the new annual card.
invalidators: Instructor/organizer kits turn out to be already saturated on Etsy
NMJL or tile-brand IP complaints against listings that reference the card
Appropriation backlash targeting non-Asian sellers of mahjong products
Etsy views fail to convert during a 3-week test
window.seasonality: Holiday hosting and Hanukkah/Christmas gifting Nov-Dec; New-Year club formation in January; a new card each year (spring release timing not verified in this session).

rights.note: Do not reproduce the National Mah Jongg League card's hands or use NMJL names/logos beyond plain compatibility statements; write original example hands. Do not copy branded tile artwork (e.g., designer sets); draw original tiles. The Mahjong Line backlash shows the risk of 'refreshing' the game or stripping Chinese characters, so credit its Chinese origins and avoid exoticizing imagery.

timing.rationale: Mainstream surge still accelerating, with the holiday hosting and gifting window open now and digital delivery instant; the generic printable niche already filled up in 2025-26.

buyerIntent.rationale: Card-bundle sales estimate, gift guides, oversubscribed classes and rising 'pdf/instructor/group' keyword estimates show people paying to learn and organize.

supplyGap.rationale: Player cheat sheets, score cards and merch are crowded; an instructor/organizer gap is plausible but unverified.

productFit.rationale: Printables and spreadsheets are easy with AI and design tools; needs careful rules accuracy and original example hands.

durability.rationale: Multi-year growth across clubs, venues and instructors; the annual card refreshes demand for organizing aids each year.

economics.rationale: Digital margins are high, but player printables sell at $1-$12; organizer/instructor kits can plausibly price higher ($12-$29). No revenue forecast implied.

candidates.actionRationale: Independent, multi-source evidence of a newcomer surge with visible purchase intent, plus a cheap digital test that can reach buyers before the holidays. Test the less crowded organizer/instructor angle, not another generic cheat sheet, and stop quickly if it gets no views.

products.buyer: New independent mahjong instructors and club hosts running beginner classes
products.theme: Beginner class kit: editable 3-session lesson handouts (tile ID, Charleston walk-through, joker basics in original wording with original practice hands), class sign-in and student progress checklist, 'first game' certificate, class flyer and social templates, and a heritage page crediting Chinese origins
products.whyBuy: Instructor searches are reported up sharply and classes are oversubscribed; a ready kit saves new teachers prep time and looks professional.
products.differentiation: Built for teachers and hosts rather than players; Canva-editable for the host's own branding; respectful heritage framing.
products.validationTest: List one $19 kit on Etsy and Gumroad with a free one-page sample; DM 20-30 instructors/club accounts on Instagram; $1-2/day Etsy ads for 14 days.
products.continueIf: At least 3 sales or at least 2% conversion on at least 300 listing views within 21 days.
products.pivotIf: Views and favorites but no sales: split into a $7 student handout pack and a $12 admin pack.
products.stopIf: Under 100 views after 3 weeks with ads, or instructor kits turn out to be abundant at lower prices.
products.rightsNote: No reproduction of NMJL card hands or logos; original tile drawings; describe compatibility in plain words only.

products.buyer: People starting or running mahjong clubs, leagues and weekly open play
products.theme: Club organizer kit: Google Sheets season standings and kitty/payout ledger, round-robin table-rotation charts for 8-32 players, sign-up and waitlist sheets, a club 'house rules' template, and printable table numbers
products.whyBuy: Club searches and attendance are reported to be exploding; organizers juggling 30-55 weekly players need rotation and record-keeping tools.
products.differentiation: Solves multi-table logistics, not single-game scoring like existing score cards.
products.validationTest: Publish at $12 with a short screen-recording demo; pin 5 Pinterest pins; track views, favorites and sales for 21 days alongside the instructor kit.
products.continueIf: At least 3 sales in 21 days or buyer messages asking for added formats.
products.pivotIf: Interest in only one piece (e.g., rotation charts): sell that piece alone at $5-7.
products.stopIf: No sales after 30 days and under 150 views.
products.rightsNote: Generic organizing tools; avoid NMJL marks in titles beyond plain description.

products.buyer: Hosts of holiday mahjong nights (Hanukkah, Christmas, New Year's Eve) and gift-givers
products.theme: Holiday mahjong night kit: invitations, place cards, first-timer table tents ('how a turn works'), score pads and a cocoa or cocktail menu card in three original holiday designs
products.whyBuy: Mahjong now appears in holiday gift guides and girls'-night hosting; a themed kit makes a game night feel like an event.
products.differentiation: Seasonal party styling plus first-timer table tents; score pads alone are already common.
products.validationTest: List by Nov 1 at $8; 10 Pinterest pins; watch favorites and sales through Dec 15.
products.pivotIf: Favorites but few sales: bundle it into the club kit as a bonus.
products.rightsNote: Original illustrations only; avoid branded tile designs and NMJL card content.

candidates.name: Hyrox / indoor fitness racing (8 x 1 km runs + 8 stations)
candidates.summary: A standardized indoor race (eight 1 km runs alternating with eight functional workout stations) that has turned gym-goers into first-time 'fitness racers' who train for months toward an event.
candidates.what: Hyrox races use the same format everywhere: 1 km run, then a station (ski erg, sled push, sled pull, burpee broad jumps, row, farmers carry, sandbag lunges, wall balls), repeated eight times. That makes times comparable and gives newcomers a concrete training target. Participants track run splits and station times and follow 8-16 week plans.

origin.text: A branded race series whose 2025/26 season is reported at more than 1.5 million athletes, with the 2026/27 calendar expanding to 107 race weekends including new US host cities.

adopters.text: Gym members, runners and CrossFit-adjacent athletes looking for a goal race; gyms affiliating to offer training (UK affiliates 18 to 120 in a year).

spread.text: Global press (Malaysia, Thailand, Australia, UK trade press, US functional-fitness media) with record single-event turnouts in Asia. US-specific participation figures were not found; US growth is shown only by new host cities.

trajectory.text: Globally surging: reported participation of 1.5M in 2025/26 with more than 2M expected in 2026/27, plus multi-week residencies for demand. The US is a smaller, growing slice (new San Diego and Portland events), so the US trajectory is less certain.

productDemand.text: People pay for preparation: several independent training books, an official-partner ebook, Notion trackers and apps exist, and sellers bundle printable checklists and calendars. That is supply-side evidence; direct sales figures were not observed.

competition.text: Moderate to high for training plans (books, Rogue ebook, apps). Narrower for physical logbooks and printable split trackers, though a logbook seller already targets the race-day log. The trademark limits keyword use for unofficial products.

gap.text: A paper or printable split-and-station logbook for first-time racers (16-week block, per-station PB tracker, compromised-run log, race-day checklist), sold as a January training gift, appears thinner than plans and apps. Training plans carry expertise and injury-liability expectations a solo creator should avoid.

window.estimate: Mid-Nov 2026 to Mar 2027 (holiday gifts, then New-Year race sign-ups); the format looks durable for multiple seasons.
window.reasoning: The 2026/27 season is underway and expanding; New-Year fitness goals line up with spring races. KDP paperbacks take days to go live and ship quickly, which fits a December listing.
invalidators: Brand enforcement against unofficial products using the name
US participation stays small relative to Europe/Asia
Apps (including official ones) make paper logs irrelevant to this tech-forward audience
window.seasonality: January resolution peak; race-specific spikes near US event dates (not verified).

rights.note: HYROX is a brand with official partners (PUMA, Rogue). Do not use the name or logo in product titles or designs. Describe the product generically ('for 8-station fitness races') and rely on descriptive keywords; any use of the name, even in tags, carries takedown risk. Avoid prescriptive training or medical claims.

timing.rationale: Season expanding and the New-Year window is close, but US-specific growth evidence is thin.

buyerIntent.rationale: Multiple paid training resources exist and participation is reported in the millions, but no direct sales data for logs.

supplyGap.rationale: Plans, apps and Notion trackers are present; a paper-log niche may be open but is unverified.

productFit.rationale: Logbooks are easy to make; the trademark limits discovery, and plans need expertise.

durability.rationale: Participation reported growing season over season, with Olympic ambitions and gym affiliate growth.

economics.rationale: KDP and printable margins are fine at $7-12; heavy competition from free apps caps pricing.

candidates.actionRationale: Real, durable participation growth, but US share, product-specific demand and how much the trademark limits keywords are unresolved. Build a generic fitness-race logbook in November for a mid-December KDP/Etsy launch aimed at New-Year racers rather than testing now.

products.buyer: First-time fitness racers training for a spring 2027 event, and gym partners buying them a gift
products.theme: 16-week fitness-race training log (KDP 6x9 paperback plus printable PDF): weekly plan grid, 8 run-split + 8 station time tracker per session, station PB pages, compromised-running log, race-day checklist and post-race reflection
products.whyBuy: A standardized format makes split tracking central to training, and January brings new sign-ups.
products.differentiation: Paper alternative to apps, focused on split and station tracking rather than prescribing workouts; no brand name used.

candidates.name: Needlepoint revival among Gen Z and millennials (stitch nights)
candidates.summary: Young women are taking up needlepoint, stitching hand-painted canvases at home and at shop 'stitch nights', driven by TikTok and a wish to put phones down.
candidates.what: Needlepoint is stitching wool or silk thread through a stiff mesh canvas, usually hand-painted by a designer. A 2024 TikTok wave pulled younger stitchers into local shops, and in 2026 beginner kits, stitch clubs and public beginner classes are spreading. Stitchers manage stashes of canvases and threads, track projects, and send finished pieces to 'finishers' (e.g., ornaments, pillows).

origin.text: A traditional craft; the youth wave is attributed by shop owners to needlepoint 'blowing up' on TikTok in 2024.

adopters.text: Gen Z and younger millennial women seeking a screen-free, social hobby; hosts of home stitch nights; shops running weekly clubs.

spread.text: From TikTok to national youth and business press (YPulse, Fortune, CBS) and regional outlets (News 12, D Magazine), and into municipal and museum beginner classes; Michaels' trend report also flags it.

trajectory.text: Coverage continues from Jan to Aug 2026 and beginner programming is spreading, but hard participation numbers are lacking; reported search growth (needlepoint +251% YoY) has unconfirmed attribution.

productDemand.text: Strong spending on physical goods (kits selling out, a multimillion-dollar needlepoint business). New tracking apps and a published journal suggest an organizing need. Demand for paid digital trackers specifically was not observed.

competition.text: Moderate: two apps (one free), a published journal and at least one Substack printable series target needlepoint organizing, plus many adjacent cross-stitch planners. The volume of needlepoint-specific printables on Etsy was not checked.

gap.text: A stylish paper/printable canvas-stash and project journal made for needlepoint workflows (mesh count, kitted status, thread by brand/number, finisher and finishing-deadline tracker for holiday ornaments and stockings) may be thinner than for cross-stitch, along with stitch-night hosting printables. Both are inference; the finishing-deadline need is an assumption about the hobby and was not checked in this session.

window.estimate: Nov 2026 to Jan 2027 (gifts for stitchers, New-Year stitch goals), then evergreen.
window.reasoning: Craft trackers sell around gifting and New-Year goals; the hobby wave has run since 2024 and still drew coverage in Aug 2026.
invalidators: Free apps (Stitchpoint) absorb the organizing need
Etsy turns out to be saturated with needlepoint journals
The youth wave cools before January
window.seasonality: Holiday gifting and ornament/stocking stitching in Q4 (assumed); New-Year goal setting in January.

rights.note: Do not reproduce designers' hand-painted canvas art or paid stitch guides; draw original motifs. Press ties the craft to celebrities, so avoid celebrity names or likenesses.

timing.rationale: The wave is established among young stitchers and Q4/New Year suits trackers, but the growth phase started in 2024.

buyerIntent.rationale: Physical kit sell-outs are reported; intent for digital trackers is unverified.

supplyGap.rationale: Fewer needlepoint-specific trackers seen than for cross-stitch, but a free app competes and Etsy was not checked.

productFit.rationale: Printable and KDP journals are straightforward; needs hobby-accurate fields.

durability.rationale: Social stitch clubs and retail investment suggest staying power beyond a fad.

economics.rationale: $6-13 printable/KDP price points; stitchers spend heavily on canvases, so price sensitivity may be low (inference).

candidates.actionRationale: The newcomer wave is real and spreading, but the evidence shows demand for physical kits, not for digital trackers, and supply wasn't fully checked. Build the stash/project journal for a mid-November launch and treat it as a low-cost test.

products.buyer: Newer needlepoint stitchers with a growing canvas and thread stash; gift-givers for stitchers
products.theme: Needlepoint project journal and canvas stash log (printable PDF plus KDP paperback): canvas inventory (designer, size, mesh, kitted Y/N, price), thread stash by brand/color number, per-project log with stitch notes, finisher tracker with due dates, and 2027 stitch goals
products.whyBuy: Stitchers who buy many canvases need to track them; apps exist, which suggests the need, but some prefer paper.
products.differentiation: Needlepoint-specific fields (mesh, kitted status, finishing) instead of generic cross-stitch planners; preppy-modern styling suited to the younger audience.
products.validationTest: List the printable at $8 by Nov 10; 10 Pinterest pins plus 3 stitch-night Instagram posts; check views and sales by Dec 10 before doing the KDP version.
products.continueIf: At least 5 sales or at least 400 views with 30+ favorites by Dec 10.
products.pivotIf: Views without sales: drop to a $4 stash-tracker-only version or bundle with the stitch-night kit.
products.rightsNote: Original decorative art only; no designer canvas images.

products.differentiation: Built for needlepoint gatherings specifically (swap tickets, project cards) rather than generic party printables.
products.validationTest: List at $6; measure views and sales over 21 days alongside the journal.
products.pivotIf: Generalize to a 'craft night' kit covering knitting and crochet groups.
